chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Muhammad ibn Hamran, from Zurarah, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both)
Regarding the woman who is divorced in a state of purity, in a single sitting, three times, he said: 'She is [considered] one [divorce].'
ai.seo_question: Does triple divorce in one sitting count as three divorces or just one in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from the Tahdhib al-Ahkam highlights the foundational Shia position of 'Tahsin al-Talaq' (counting triple divorce as one) when pronounced in a single sitting during a period of purity, contrasting with the Sunni view of 'Tajmi' (counting as three). It underscores the legal nuance that the husband retains the right of 'Rujua' (revocation) without requiring a new marriage contract, a key distinction in Ja'fari jurisprudence. The chain of transmission through Zurara and Ibn Humran adds weight to this ruling within the primary hadith corpus.
